title: Instrumentation sprint proposal: multi-model routing observability
content:
TL;DR:
This doc proposes a focused 2-week instrumentation sprint to add observability for the multi-model routing feature (fanout + dynamic routing to model variants). Goal: be able to detect routing regressions, quantify routing-induced latency/cost, and provide operators with actionable dashboards and a lightweight trace sampling policy.

Background / Why now:
- Multi-model routing landed in staging last week; we saw early performance variance across tenants.
- Routing decisions (region, model-size, quantized variant) add new failure and latency modes that are not visible in current dashboards.
- Early customers will be able to pin routing policies; we need telemetry before GA to avoid surprise cost/latency regressions.

Sprint goals (measurable):
1) Metric coverage: produce 8 new metrics + 4 derived SLI calculations to cover routing correctness, cost, and latency.
2) Tracing: add span annotations for routing decision points and implement a sampled trace path that includes model selection, KV-cache hit flags, and fallbacks.
3) Dashboards: ship a triage dashboard (compact) + a rollout readiness panel for product owners.
4) Alerting: define 2 alert signals (routing-variance, fallback-rate) with playbooks.

Non-goals:
- Full rollout of synthetic probes (future sprint).
- End-to-end billing attribution (approximate cost metrics only).

Metric definitions (proposal):
- routing.decision.count (counter): increment for every routing decision. Tags: route_reason, tenant_id, model_family, target_variant. Use to compute distribution of decisions.
- routing.latency.p95_ms (histogram-derived gauge): per-routing-decision latency for model selection step (not token generation).
- routing.kv_cache.prefetch_hit_rate (gauge pct): rolling 5m ratio of prefetch hits on candidate model KV caches.
- routing.fallback.rate_1m (gauge %): fraction of requests in past minute that used fallback variant due to capacity/timeout.
- routing.cost.estimated_tokens (counter): estimated token-equivalent cost delta introduced by routing variant (approx).
- routing.staleness.mismatch_count (counter): count of requests where client pinned version but engine routed to newer compatible variant (indicator of mismatch).
- routing.quality.regression_score (gauge): synthetic prompt-set regression score per rollout cohort (integration point with Optimize).
- routing.multi_model.fanout_ratio (gauge): average fanout (# of model candidates evaluated / final chosen) per request.

Derived SLIs (examples):
- slo.routing.latency: 95th percentile end-to-end routing decision time <= 20ms in 99th percentile of tenants. (Query across routing.latency.p95_ms with tenant filter).
- slo.routing.fallback: fallback.rate_1m <= 1% per tenant.
- slo.routing.cost-variance: estimated cost delta / baseline <= 15% for 95% of requests.

Metric instrumentation notes / tags:
- Always emit tenant_id and route_request_id for correlation.
- model_family tag should be canonicalized (e.g., llama2-70b, redwood-mini-v1).
- route_reason: {latency_slo, cost_save, region_affinity, pinned_version} - small set to reduce cardinality.
- Avoid including free-form prompt text. If prompt fingerprint required, use 128-bit hash and only when allowed.

Tracing strategy (proposal):
- New span "route.selection" (duration covers model selection algorithm runtime). Fields: route_request_id, candidate_list (IDs, truncated), decision_reason, selected_variant, kv_prefetch_status (hit|miss|unknown), tenant_id.
- Child spans: "candidate.evaluate" for heavy-weight candidate scoring (only sampled for 1% by default).
- Token-generation spans remain as today; ensure trace correlation via route_request_id -> generation_request_id mapping.
- Sampling policy: adaptive sampling: always sample traces with fallback.rate or error code != 0; otherwise sample 1% of non-error requests. Provide a button in the dashboard to temporarily increase sampling for a tenant.
- Span size limits: cap candidate_list to 8 entries; serialize as comma-separated IDs to control size. Do not attach model weights or configs.

Dashboard notes (triage dashboard - compact):
Panels (compact layout for oncall):
1) Routing overview: bar chart of route_reason distribution (top 5) + trend (1h, 24h).
2) Latency heatmap: routing.latency p50/p95/p99 by tenant cohort.
3) Fallback funnel: fallback.rate_1m + trace anchor list (links to sampled traces).
4) Cost delta: routing.cost.estimated_tokens aggregated per tenant, shown as sparkline + top-10 tenants by delta.
5) Fanout distribution: histogram of fanout_ratio and its median.
6) KV-prefetch health: prefetch_hit_rate by model_family.
7) Recent anomalous traces: top 25 sampled traces with tag fallback=true or decision_reason=timeout.

Dashboard implementation guidance:
- Make panel queries efficient: use preaggregations for routing.decision.count and routing.cost.* (rollups every 1m).
- Default view should be global; provide tenant drilldown via a tenant selector.
- Add a small control to raise trace sampling to 100% for selected tenant for 10 minutes (operators only).

Alerting & runbook (initial):
- alert: routing-fallback-spike
  - trigger: fallback.rate_1m > 5% for 3 consecutive 5m windows for any tenant with >100 req/min.
  - severity: P2 (depends on tenant SLA).
  - runbook quick steps: check region capacity -> check model pool utilization -> open trace links -> escalate to serving-runtime oncall if trend persists.
  - pager: eng-serving-runtime + eng-observability.

- alert: routing-latency-regression
  - trigger: routing.latency.p95_ms increase > 3x baseline and sustained for 10m.
  - actions: pull traces, check candidate.evaluate span durations, inspect KV-prefetch hit rate.

Queries & cost considerations:
- Keep high-cardinality tags limited (no free-form reason).
- Rollups: 1m and 5m rollups for counts and estimated cost only.
- Traces are more expensive; use adaptive sampling and a short retention for sampled traces (14d default).

Rollout gating / telemetry gating for GA:
- Required signals before GA: routing.decision.count present + rollup, routing.fallback.rate_1m, routing.latency.p95_ms, KV-prefetch hit rate.
- Minimum dashboard: triage panel + tenant drilldown.
- Alerting: routing-fallback-spike and routing-latency-regression configured.

Timeline (2-week sprint):
Week 1:
- Day 1-2: Metric naming + tagging schema + instrumentation API changes (eng-serving-runtime). Ticket ENG-1423.
- Day 3-5: Implement route.selection span and basic sampling hooks.
- Day 5: First pass dashboard skeleton (observability team).
Week 2:
- Day 6-9: Add derived SLIs, rollups, and alerts. End-to-end test with staging traffic.
- Day 10: Oncall tabletop walkthrough; finalize runbooks.
- Day 11: Buffer + doc polish and handoff.

Action items (owners):
- Rohan Iyer: finalize metric tag list + implement routing.decision.count and rollups (ENG-1423).
- Elena Morales: trace span schema + sampling changes, ensure route_request_id propagation (PR link in linked_artifacts).
- Samir Gupta: dashboard panels + tenant drilldown prototyping.
- Maya Chen: sprint coordination, alert/playbook authoring, and GA readiness checklist.

Open questions / risks:
- Cardinality risk from tenant_id and model_family combination. Mitigation: limit cardinality by requiring model_family canonicalization and only enabling tenant_id high-cardinality panels behind filters.
- Cost estimation in routing.cost.estimated_tokens is approximate; needs product alignment on cost model. Action: sync with finance (OBS-2217).
- Do we need to store candidate scoring vectors for debug? Risk: PII/security and size. Recommendation: avoid persistent storing; include truncated top-3 candidate IDs in spans.

Notes to reviewers:
- Prefer conservative instrumentation first (counters + small spans) and iterate if gaps found during staging.
- Keep instrumentation ID formats stable — metric names and tag keys are contract surfaces for dashboards and alerts.

Appendix: quick sample queries (pseudo-sql):
- fallback rate per tenant: sum(routing.fallback.count) / sum(routing.decision.count) by tenant over last 1m
- p95 routing latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(routing.latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant))

End.
